question.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(5,\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample 

$$
{x}_{1}=5,\,{x}_{2}=3,\,{x}_{3}=2,\,{x}_{4}=1.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡a+b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +c\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=5$ as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{N}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{N-x},\,x=0,1,…,N \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{5-x},\,x=0,1,…,5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{5-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{5-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(5-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(5-{x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(5n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

Now, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{1}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{2}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{3}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{4}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, our expression for $l(\theta )$ becomes

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}))+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(5n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{5})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{3})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}) \\  & =1\cdot 10\cdot 10\cdot 5 \\  & =500,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
S=5+3+2+1=11.
$$

Substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta )$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(500)+11\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(5\cdot 4-11)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(500)+11\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +9\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=500+11+9=520.
$$
